findings.message: topic-02.mdx:24-25 presents an attributed quotation as documented fact: After the 2012 fire, a Karachi factory owner told a reporter, "We had safety measures. We had a fire extinguisher." No source is cited, and the sources/unit-04.md Unverifiable-sources declaration covers only the fire's public-record facts (September 2012, more than 250 workers killed behind locked and barred exits) and the unit's own framework reading. The style guide (specs/content/style-guide.md, Citation format) requires quotations under 15 words to carry a citation to a named source. This 9-word quote is an attributed real-world utterance, not a fictional-narrative device like the uncle's dialogue, so it states more than the declaration supports. Repair: cite a verifiable report, or reframe as an illustrative hypothetical (for example, an owner defending his factory might say), or extend the declaration to cover it honestly.

The WHO Deafness and hearing loss fact sheet (who-hearing-2026, verified by direct fetch 2026-09-23 with a bound excerpt at sources/texts/who-hearing-2026.md) is cited in topic-07.mdx:45-46 ("the hearing loss the WHO counts in the hundreds of millions (WHO, 2026)") and listed in topic-07.mdx:156-157 Further reading, but has no row in sources/unit-04.md and no coverage/unit-04.md row. This violates the sources-consulted contract stated in sources/unit-04.md itself ("every key cited in ... the unit's per-topic ## Further reading sections appears here"). The claim itself is supported by the bound excerpt (about 430 million people require rehabilitation for disabling hearing loss; loud noise a named cause), so the repair is declarative: add the who-hearing-2026 row to sources/unit-04.md (and a U4-13 coverage row if the mapping is intended), and note in the row that the figure is all-cause hearing loss with noise a named cause.

The abbasi2022 mapping for U4-09 claims support that does not exist in the unit. sources/unit-04.md says abbasi2022 supports "topic-05.mdx U4-09 (bottom-of-hierarchy reliance in practice)", and coverage/unit-04.md maps U4-09 in topic-05.mdx to abbasi2022 plus a reinforcement row "U4-09 | unit-teacher-notes.mdx | Managing the activities | abbasi2022". Neither topic-05.mdx nor unit-teacher-notes.mdx cites abbasi2022 anywhere (grep verified), and neither contains the described bottom-of-hierarchy content; that finding lives in Unit 3 (per the excerpt's own support note). The mapping appears copied from Unit 3. Repair: correct the coverage row, the reinforcement row and the sources Supports cell to the actual grounding of U4-09 (measures and models are taught from general disciplinary knowledge with harrington-gill at title level), or add the claimed content with a proper citation.

coverage/unit-04.md and sources/unit-04.md over-claim who-occupational-health as the grounding source for U4-03, U4-04, U4-06, U4-08, U4-12, U4-14 and U4-15. The bound excerpt (sources/texts/who-occupational-health.md: definition, three objectives, disciplines, named concerns) contains no passage on OSH management systems, ILO C155/ISO 45001/PDCA, regulatory instruments, duties and rights, management principles, HSE plans, the external environment or HSE tools, and the topic bodies for those sub-topics (topic-02, topic-03, topic-04, topic-05, topic-06, topic-07) never cite WHO in prose; only the U4-01 mapping (services-sector concerns incl. mental health) is excerpt-supported and body-cited. Similarly who-mental-health-work is mapped to U4-10 in topic-05.mdx but topic-05 never cites it (the excerpt is topically related: poor working environments pose mental health risks). The depth gate checks sources-coverage scope agreement and excerpt existence, not per-passage support, so this passed G2. Repair: either add in-body citations where the WHO pages genuinely support a specific claim, or re-ground those coverage rows honestly (the content is standard disciplinary knowledge presented without citation; harrington-gill is the guide's title-level reference). As it stands the governance tables misrepresent the unit's evidentiary basis for 8 of 15 sub-topics.

topic-01.mdx:63-64 calls the 2012 Karachi fire "one of the deadliest industrial fires anywhere on record". The toll (more than 250) makes this defensible public record, but it is a comparative superlative beyond the facts the Unverifiable-sources declaration names (date, toll, locked exits). Consider softening to the declared facts or extending the declaration to cover the characterization.

topic-02.mdx:40-42 states Pakistan's national framework was "strengthened in recent decades by the ILO's post-fire programmes". This is a real, well-documented institutional response, but it is an uncited factual characterization tied to the fire narrative and not covered by the declaration. Consider citing an ILO source or declaring it alongside the fire entry.

topic-03.mdx:48-51 places the abbasi2022 citation at the end of a sentence whose second half is the unit's own inference ("a reminder that enforcement works best when the people exposed are part of it"). The excerpt supports the study's method (community consultation beside site visits), not an enforcement-effectiveness finding. Consider splitting the sentence so the citation scopes only to the method claim.
topic-04.mdx:75 says "the Karachi fire's factories had paperwork too" (plural). The 2012 fire was one factory. Consider "the Karachi fire's factory" or "factories like the one in the Karachi fire".

topic-07.mdx:41-42 references the 2015 Karachi heatwave ("demonstrated at city scale") as an undeclared public-record event. Unlike the 2012 fire it states no toll and no specifics, so it is acceptable as general public record; for consistency with the fire treatment, consider a one-line declaration in sources/unit-04.md.
